description: Fictional multi-speaker meeting transcripts for scoring on-device meeting-notes models. An expected item is retained when the generated notes contain at least one anyOf string and every allOf string (case-insensitive substring).

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Okay, morning everyone. Let's keep this quick, we've got the design review at ten.

segments.speaker: Tomas
segments.text: Sure. Uh, I can go first.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Go ahead, Tomas.

segments.speaker: Tomas
segments.text: So yesterday I finished the export fix. The CSV export was dropping rows past 500, and that's merged now.

segments.speaker: Ingrid
segments.text: Nice. Was that the bug from the Halvorsen account?

segments.speaker: Tomas
segments.text: Yeah, that one. Today I'm on the sync timeout. It's set to 30 seconds and we're seeing failures on, um, slower connections.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: What do you want to raise it to?

segments.speaker: Tomas
segments.text: I'd say 90 seconds. Retries stay at three.

segments.speaker: Marisol
segments.text: Is 90 too long? Like, the spinner just sits there.

segments.speaker: Tomas
segments.text: We show progress after ten seconds now, so it's not a dead screen.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Okay, let's do it. We raise the sync timeout to 90 seconds. Decision made, nobody argue.

segments.speaker: Marisol
segments.text: No argument from me.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Ingrid?

segments.speaker: Ingrid
segments.text: So I, uh, I finished the onboarding mockups. There are 12 screens now, down from 17.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: That's a big cut.

segments.speaker: Ingrid
segments.text: It is. We merged the bank connection steps into one. I need feedback by Thursday, March 6th, so I can hand off to engineering on Friday.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: I'll review the onboarding mockups today.

segments.speaker: Ingrid
segments.text: Thanks. And Marisol, I need you to check the empty states on those.

segments.speaker: Marisol
segments.text: Sure, I'll add the empty states to the test plan.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Marisol, your update?

segments.speaker: Marisol
segments.text: Yeah. So the regression run last night was 214 tests, four failures. Three are flaky, um, the date picker ones again.

segments.speaker: Tomas
segments.text: The date picker, of course.

segments.speaker: Marisol
segments.text: And one is real. Refunds over $1,000 show the wrong tax line on the receipt.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Wait, on the receipt or in the ledger?

segments.speaker: Marisol
segments.text: Just the receipt. The ledger is right.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Is that a release blocker?

segments.speaker: Marisol
segments.text: I think so, yeah. It's customer facing and it's money.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Agreed. So we hold the 4.2 release until the refund tax bug is fixed.

segments.speaker: Tomas
segments.text: I can take the refund bug after the timeout change. Should be done tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Great. Tomas fixes the refund tax line, Marisol retests it.

segments.speaker: Marisol
segments.text: And I'll rerun the full suite after.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Perfect. If that's clean we ship 4.2 on March 11th instead of today.

segments.speaker: Ingrid
segments.text: Do support know it's moving?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Not yet. I'll tell them right after this.

segments.speaker: Ingrid
segments.text: Okay. And Priya, do you want the mockups in Figma or should I walk you through them?

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Figma's fine, I'll leave comments. If anything's confusing, I'll grab you after lunch.

segments.speaker: Tomas
segments.text: Oh, one more thing from me. The Android build is failing on the staging pipeline. I think it's a certificate issue. I'll ping infra, it's not blocking anything yet.

segments.speaker: Marisol
segments.text: Is that why my test devices didn't get the new build this morning?

segments.speaker: Tomas
segments.text: Probably, yeah. Sorry. I'll post in the channel when it's fixed.

segments.speaker: Priya
segments.text: Okay. Anything else? No? Great, see you all at the review.

decisions.label: hold 4.2 release until refund tax bug is fixed

actions.label: Tomas fixes the refund tax bug
Priya reviews the onboarding mockups
Marisol adds empty states to the test plan

meetings.title: Kestrel Freight expansion and renewal call

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Hi Graham, hi Lucia. Thanks for making time. Can you hear me okay?

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Yeah, we've got you. Lucia's here with me in the room.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Hi Nadia.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Great. I've got Owen with me, he's our solutions engineer at Brightwater, he'll cover the technical side.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: Hey everyone. Good to finally put faces to the emails.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: So, um, the plan for today. We wanted to go over the expansion, the pricing, and the renewal timeline, and then Owen has a couple of things on single sign-on and data residency.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Sounds good.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: So, just to recap where we are. Kestrel Freight is on 180 seats today, and your renewal date is April 1st.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Correct. April 1st.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: And Graham, you mentioned last time you wanted to bring the dispatch teams in the Memphis and Tulsa yards onto the platform.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Right. That's, uh, about sixty more people. So we'd go to 240 seats.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: 240. Okay, great. And that's dispatchers only, or the yard supervisors too?

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Both. The supervisors are maybe a dozen of the sixty.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Got it. So, pricing. On the current contract you're at $42 per seat per month. For the expansion, we can bring the whole account down to $38 per seat per month if you sign for 240 seats on a two year term.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Two years is longer than we usually do.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: I understand. The one year price would be $40 per seat.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Okay. And what's the annual total at 38?

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: At 240 seats and $38 a seat, it comes to $109,440 a year.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: One oh nine, okay. Let me write that down. And is that billed annually or quarterly?

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Annually by default. We can do quarterly, but then it's the $40 rate.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Annual is fine. And the discount we talked about in January, the 15 percent on onboarding services?

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Right. So I want to be really clear about that one. That 15 percent discount on the services package is valid through the end of March. We are not extending the discount past March.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Even if procurement takes longer on our end?

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: I'm afraid so. It's tied to our quarter, and I don't have room to move it. I'd rather tell you now than surprise you in April.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Okay. I appreciate that, honestly.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: What's in the services package again? Remind me.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: It's the onboarding bundle. Data migration from your old dispatch system, two admin training sessions, and the dispatcher workshops.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: And the workshops are on site, so for Memphis and Tulsa we'd fly someone out.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: That'd be useful. Those teams are, uh, they're not the most tech friendly crowd.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: We hear that a lot. Usually after the first workshop people stop calling the old system "the real one."

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Ha. We'll see.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: How long is the data migration? Our old system has, I think, eleven years of load history.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: Eleven years is fine. Most of the time is mapping the fields, not moving the data. Usually about two weeks end to end.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Okay.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: So, timeline. If legal signs by Friday, we start onboarding on March 3rd. That gives the yards about four weeks before the renewal kicks in on April 1st.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: And if legal doesn't sign by Friday?

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Then we'd start, um, probably the week after, but I can't promise March 3rd. Our onboarding team books up pretty fast this time of year.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Okay. Our legal team has the MSA now. The sticking point is the data processing addendum.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: That's actually a good segue into my part.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: So on the technical side, two things. SSO and data residency. For SSO, you're on Okta, right?

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: We are. Well, mostly. The Tulsa yard still has some local accounts.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: That's fine, we can run both during the transition. We support SAML through Okta. Setup usually takes about an hour once your IT team has the metadata. I'll send you our SSO setup guide by Wednesday.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Perfect. Send it to me and I'll forward it to our IT folks.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: On data residency, all of your data stays in our US East region. We don't replicate outside the US.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: That's the exact wording legal wanted. Can you put that in writing?

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: Yes, it's in the DPA already, section four. I'll highlight it when I send the guide.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Okay. That might actually unblock them.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: What about uptime? Last year we had that, uh, that outage in November.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: Yeah. I remember that one. Our SLA is 99.9 percent monthly uptime, and for November we were under that, so we credited the month.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Right, we did get the credit.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: And since then we've added a second region for failover. So the same failure today wouldn't take you down.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Okay, good. That was a bad Tuesday for us.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: While I have you, there's one thing the dispatchers keep asking about. Route optimization. Is that coming?

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: So, um, I want to be careful here. It's on our roadmap, but I can't commit to a date, and I don't want you to buy based on it.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Fair enough.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: What I can say is the routing API is in a private preview. If you want, I can see if Kestrel can join the preview.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Yeah, we'd be interested. No promises needed.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: Okay. I'll ask the product team, no commitment either way.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: One more on pricing. If we add seats mid term, what's the price?

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Same per seat price, $38, prorated to the renewal.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: And if we go down in seats?

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: We, uh, we don't do mid term reductions. You can reduce at the renewal.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Okay. That's standard, I figured.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Can we get admin access for more people? Right now only two of us have it, and I'm the bottleneck for everything.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: Sure. How many admins do you want?

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Probably five. One per yard, plus me and Lucia.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: That's fine, no extra cost. Just send me the list with their emails.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: I'll send the admin list by Monday.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Oh, and reporting. Our CFO wants a monthly usage report. Is that something we can pull ourselves?

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: Yes. There's a usage dashboard in the admin console, and you can schedule it as a PDF to go out on the first of every month.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Great. That's one less spreadsheet.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: On the training sessions, can those be recorded? We have a lot of turnover on the night shift, and I don't want to book a new session every time someone starts.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: Yes, we record them, and you'd keep the recordings. We also have short videos in the help center, they're about five minutes each.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Good. The night shift will actually watch five minutes. An hour, no.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Who would our day to day contact be after onboarding? Is that you, Nadia?

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: For commercial things, yes, me. For anything technical, you'd have a named customer success manager. Right now that would be Priyanka on our team, she covers most of our logistics customers.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Okay. Can we meet her before we sign?

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Absolutely. I'll set up a short intro call with her next week.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: And for the Memphis yard, the internet there is, um, not great. Does the app work on a slow connection?

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: It works, it's just slower to load the map views. The dispatch board itself is pretty light. If you want, I can run a quick test from their network before the workshop.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: That'd be great, actually. I'll get you a contact at the yard.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: And invoices. Right now they go to Graham, and they really should go to accounts payable.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Easy fix. Send me the AP email and I'll change it on the new order form.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: I'll send it over with the redlines.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Sorry, one more. If we, uh, if we ever wanted to leave, how do we get our data out?

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: Full export at any time, CSV or through the API. It's in the contract, no fee for it.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: Okay. Not planning to, just, you know, I get asked.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Okay, so let me recap what I've got, just so we're all on the same page.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: I'll send a revised order form with 240 seats at $38 on a two year term, today if possible, tomorrow at the latest.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Tomorrow's fine.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Owen sends the SSO setup guide by Wednesday, with the residency section highlighted.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: Yep.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Lucia, you'll take the DPA language back to legal and send us their redlines.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Yes, I'll send the redlines as soon as I get them. Hopefully Thursday.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Graham sends the admin list by Monday. And the plan is, if legal signs by Friday, onboarding starts March 3rd.

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: That works for us.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: And just to repeat it, so nobody's surprised later, the 15 percent services discount ends in March. We are not extending it.

segments.speaker: Lucia
segments.text: Understood. I'll make sure legal knows that too.

segments.speaker: Nadia
segments.text: Great. Anything else from your side?

segments.speaker: Graham
segments.text: No, I think that's it. Thanks, both of you.

segments.speaker: Owen
segments.text: Thanks everyone. Talk soon.

dates.label: onboarding start March 3 if legal signs

decisions.label: 15 percent discount is not extended past March
conditional: if legal signs by Friday, onboarding starts March 3
account expands to 240 seats on a two-year term

actions.label: Nadia sends revised order form
Owen sends SSO setup guide by Wednesday
Lucia sends legal redlines on the DPA
Graham sends admin list by Monday

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Okay, let's get going, I've got a hard stop at two thirty. Felix, do you want to start with the pipeline?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Sure. So for the senior backend role, we have eight, no, sorry, 18 applicants who passed the resume screen this week.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Eighteen? That's way up from last month.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Yeah, the new posting is working. Putting the salary range in the listing helped a lot, people self select.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: How many of those have done the phone screen?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Seven so far. Four moved on to the technical interview, and two are scheduled for next week.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: I did two of the technical interviews. One was, um, really strong. The other one struggled with the concurrency question.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: The queue question?

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Yeah, the queue one. Which, honestly, maybe the question is too hard for a forty five minute slot.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Let's talk about that at the end. Felix, keep going.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: So the big one is Joon Park. He finished the onsite on Monday and the panel feedback is all in.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: And?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Four out of four yes. Two strong yes.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: I was one of the strong yeses. His system design round was the best I've seen this year. He actually asked about our failure modes before drawing anything.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Okay. That matches what I heard from Dmitri. So, are we ready to make an offer?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: I think we should, and quickly. He told me he has another offer that expires next week.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: What's he asking?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: He's currently at 160 base. He's asking for 175.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Where's our band for senior?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: The band tops out at 180. Midpoint is about 168.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: I'd like to come in at $172,000 base. That's above midpoint, and it leaves room for a raise at the first review.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: He might push back. Can we add a signing bonus?

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: How much would close the gap?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: I'd say $10,000 signing. That gets his first year above what he asked for.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Okay. I'm fine with that. So the decision is, we offer Joon Park $172,000 base plus a $10,000 signing bonus.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Agreed.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: And for the start date, he asked for May 5th. He wants to give his current team three weeks.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: May 5th is good. That's actually ideal, it's right after the planning cycle.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Great. I'll send the offer letter by Thursday, April 17th. I need the signing bonus approved before I can send.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: I'll get the bonus approved by finance by Wednesday. I'll message Carla today.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Thanks, Renata. One question on Joon. Do we offer remote or hybrid? He lives about an hour away.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Hybrid, two days in the office. That's the same as the rest of the team. If he pushes on it, we can talk, but let's start there.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: He mentioned at the onsite that two days is fine. He actually likes the office.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Okay, I'll write it up as hybrid.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Who's going to be his onboarding buddy? I can do it, but I'm on call the week of the fifth.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Let's ask Dmitri. Imani, you do the second week.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Works for me.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Okay. What about the other senior candidates? The ones behind Joon.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: So we have three candidates who passed the technical interview and are ready for onsites. Hannah Brooks, Teo Alvarez, and, um, Samir Haddad.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Samir's the one from the payments company?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Do we still want three more onsites if Joon accepts?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: I'd say yes. We have two senior backend openings, not one. Joon fills one of them.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Right, I forgot we got the second one approved. Okay, then yes.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Imani, can you schedule the onsites? The panel needs at least one person from platform.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Yeah. I'll schedule all three onsites for next week. I'll pull in Ravi from platform.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Good. Make sure each panel has someone who hasn't interviewed for us before. We need more trained interviewers.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Okay, I'll pair a new interviewer with a regular on each panel.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Okay, the designer role. Felix?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: So, for product designer, the pipeline is smaller. Nine applicants total, and one finalist, Sofia Mendez.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: I liked her portfolio a lot. The logistics dashboard case study especially.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Me too. But I want to see how she handles critique. Can we do a portfolio review with the design team?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Yes. I can set up a final portfolio review on April 22nd. That's the earliest the design team is free.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: April 22nd. Okay, let's do that. Is she okay waiting that long?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: She said she's not in a rush. She's currently at an agency and her contract runs through June.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Also, for Sofia, can someone from engineering sit in on the portfolio review? Designers here work really closely with us.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Good idea. You go, if you're free.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: I'll make time.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Good. So, the junior role. I know we talked about opening a junior backend position.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: I'd really like one. We have so much small stuff that a junior could own.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: I hear you. But I talked to finance this morning, and we are not opening the junior role this quarter. Maybe next quarter, if the two senior hires land.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Okay. That's, um, that's disappointing, but I get it.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Should I tell the two internal referrals? They've been asking.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Yes, please let them know it's paused, not cancelled. And keep their resumes.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Will do. I'll email both of them this week.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Now, Imani, the concurrency question. You said it's too hard?

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: I think it's the wrong question. It tests whether you've seen that exact problem before. Joon had, so he crushed it, but I don't think it predicts much.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Candidates mention it in the feedback survey too. Three of the last five said it felt like a trick question.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Okay. What would you replace it with?

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Something closer to our actual work. Like, debugging a slow endpoint with real logs. We could use a sanitized version of the incident from February.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: I like that. Can you write it up?

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Yeah. I'll draft a replacement interview question and send it to you by April 25th.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Okay, and then we test it on two internal people before we use it with candidates.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Sure.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Quick thing on time to hire. We're averaging 34 days from first screen to offer. The goal is under 30.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Where's the time going?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Mostly scheduling the onsites. Panels take about ten days to book.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: That's on us. Engineers decline the invites and don't suggest another slot.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Okay. I'll bring that up at the engineering all hands. Interview slots are part of the job.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Thank you. That would help a lot.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Anything else? Felix?

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Just one reminder. The referral bonus went up to $3,000 this quarter, so please tell your teams.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Oh, nice. I'll put it in the team channel.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Okay. So, to sum up. Felix sends the Joon Park offer by April 17th once I get the bonus approved. Imani schedules three onsites and drafts the new question. Sofia's portfolio review is on April 22nd. And no junior role this quarter.

segments.speaker: Felix
segments.text: Got it.

segments.speaker: Imani
segments.text: Sounds good.

segments.speaker: Renata
segments.text: Great, thanks both. See you next week.

decisions.label: offer Joon Park $172,000 base plus signing bonus
not opening the junior role this quarter
hold three more onsites for second senior opening

Renata gets signing bonus approved by Wednesday
Imani schedules three onsites next week
Imani drafts replacement interview question by April 25
Felix emails internal referrals that junior role is paused

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay, I think everyone's here. Tobias, are you on?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Yeah, I'm here. Sorry, my camera's being weird today.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: No problem. So, um, this is the Q3 planning session for Cairn.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: We have six things on the agenda. Roadmap, budget, hiring, the launch date, the support backlog, and risks.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: I want to give each about five minutes, so let's be disciplined. If something needs a longer conversation, we park it and I'll set up a separate meeting. I'd rather finish the whole agenda than go deep on one item.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Famous last words.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: I know, I know. Okay, roadmap first. Arjun, do you want to start?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Sure. So the big item for Q3 is offline mode.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Field technicians keep losing work when they drop signal, and it's the number one complaint in the app reviews. We have technicians in basements, in rural areas, in hospitals with no reception at all, and right now the app just, um, it just gives up on them.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: It's the number one complaint in support too. By a lot.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Right. So my proposal is that we put 40 percent of engineering capacity on offline mode for the quarter.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Forty percent of the whole team?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Of the whole team, yeah. That's roughly, uh, nine of our twenty two engineers.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: And what does that push out?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Mostly the Gantt view. The scheduling team wanted it, but honestly it's a big build. It's at least a quarter on its own.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Sales has been asking about the Gantt view, though. A couple of the enterprise prospects brought it up.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: I know. But we can't do both well. We'd end up with two half-finished things.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Which prospects?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Hollis Utilities and, uh, the county one. Brennan County.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Did either of them make it a requirement?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Brennan said nice to have. Hollis didn't say.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Then I'm going to make the call. We are not building the Gantt view this quarter. Offline mode gets the 40 percent.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Okay. I'll let sales know so they stop promising it.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Please do. And it's not dead, it's just not Q3.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Kofi, Beatriz, anything on roadmap?

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Just, um, does offline mode change the hiring plan? Like, do we need a mobile specialist?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Maybe. Let's hold that for the hiring section.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: From support, the other thing is the, uh, the recurring jobs bug.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Customers who set up weekly jobs see duplicates after the clocks change.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: That's on the list. It's small. We'll fix it in the next maintenance release.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Okay, good. Because it comes back every spring and every fall.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: And the 3.0 launch, just so everyone has the baseline, is currently June 2nd.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: We'll come back to whether that holds in the launch section.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Yeah, I have, uh, I have thoughts on that one.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Later. Arjun, can you get me a written spec for offline mode?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Yes. I'll have the offline mode spec done by May 9th.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: May 9th. Great.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Can the spec include a rough cost? Like, if it needs new sync infrastructure, I want to see that before the budget is locked.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Sure. I'll add an infrastructure estimate section.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: And a one paragraph summary I can actually use in marketing would be nice.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Ha. Okay, a paragraph for Tobias. Noted.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Does offline mode change our storage costs on the device side? Like, do customers need bigger phones?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: No. We cache the next three days of jobs. It's small. A few megabytes for most technicians.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Okay. That's fine then.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: What about the tablet app? Does offline mode ship on tablets at the same time?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Phones first. Tablets about a month later. It's the same code, but the layouts need work.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Most of the complaints are from phones anyway.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Phones first is fine.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Is there anything on the roadmap for the admin console? I keep hearing from our own ops team.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Small stuff. Bulk user import is in. Custom roles are not.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: That's fine for now. Anything else on the roadmap?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Just a note that the customer advisory board meets in, um, two weeks. I'd like to show them the offline mode designs.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Good idea, if the designs are ready. Arjun?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: They'll be rough, but yes.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: One more roadmap question, Arjun. How are we handling conflicts in offline mode? Like, what does the technician actually see when something didn't sync?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: So the plan is a small banner on the job card. It says the job has changes waiting to upload, and it shows the time of the last successful sync.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: If there's a conflict, the dispatcher picks which version wins, not the technician. Technicians are in the field, they shouldn't be resolving merge problems.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Can the dispatcher see both versions side by side? That's going to be the first thing they ask for.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: That's the plan, yeah. Side by side, with the differences highlighted. It's in the designs already.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: And photos? Technicians attach a lot of photos to jobs. Do those wait too?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Photos queue up and upload when the signal comes back. We compress them on the phone first, so it's not, uh, it's not going to eat anyone's data plan.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Who pays for the extra storage if every technician uploads a hundred photos a day?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: We already store those photos today. Offline doesn't change the volume, just the timing.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Okay. Then I don't care.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Is there a way to tell a technician they're offline before they start a job? Like, a warning?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: There's an indicator in the header. A grey cloud when you're offline. We tested a pop-up and people hated it, they just tapped it away without reading.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Good. No pop-ups.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: From the support side, I'd love a way to see a technician's sync queue from the admin console. When a customer calls and says their work vanished, we have no way to check right now.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: That's a good one. It's not in the spec yet. I'll add a read-only sync queue view for support, and we can decide later whether it makes the first release.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Will technicians need training for any of this, or is it supposed to just work?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: It should just work. The only new thing they see is the cloud icon, and maybe the banner. If they need training, we designed it wrong.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: For the advisory board, can we show a short video instead of static screens? It lands much better with that group.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: If the prototype is stable enough, sure. I'll record something rough on my phone.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Let's keep moving, we're already a little over on roadmap.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Let's move on to budget. Maya.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Okay. So, the headline. The total Q3 operating budget is $1.2 million. That's flat with Q2.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Flat even with the offline work?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Flat. Which means something has to give somewhere else. I went through every line last week, and there are really only three places where the numbers moved enough to matter, so I'll walk through those.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: The biggest change is cloud. Our cloud spend is up 22 percent quarter over quarter.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: That's mostly the new search cluster. And, um, logs. We keep way too many logs.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Whatever it is, I need it to stop growing that fast.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: We can cut log retention from ninety days to thirty. That alone is meaningful.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Good. Please do that.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Okay. I'll check with Beatriz first, support sometimes needs the old logs.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Thirty days is fine for us. We almost never go further back.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Second, marketing. Tobias, your Q3 line is $310,000.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: That's, uh, that's less than I asked for.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: It is. You asked for three sixty.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Right. Okay. Most of it is the launch anyway. If the launch date moves, the spend moves with it.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Understood. We can shift it inside the quarter, just not grow it.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Okay. Can I at least keep the trade show in September?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: The trade show is in the 310. You decide what goes.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Fine. I'll make it work.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Third, contractors. We've got three engineering contractors on the integrations work.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: I'm proposing we cut engineering contractor spend by $80,000 this quarter.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: That's basically two of the three.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: I can live with that if the integrations work slips to Q4. The Salesforce connector is the only one that's really urgent.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: The Salesforce one is the one sales cares about, so that's fine.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Decision: we cut engineering contractor spend by $80,000, and the integrations other than Salesforce move to Q4.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Does that affect support contractors? Because Beatriz is going to ask.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: I am absolutely going to ask.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: No. This is engineering contractors only. Support is a separate line, we'll get to that.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Okay, good.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Maya, what about extra engineers? I know Arjun wants more.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: I always want more.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: So here's where I land. If ARR passes $9 million by the end of June, we hire two more engineers in Q3.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: If it doesn't, we wait until Q4 and look again.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Where are we now?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: About $8.6 million.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: So we need roughly $400,000 in new ARR in about seven weeks.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Roughly, yes. It's doable but it's not certain.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: And if we hit it, can I start interviewing before July? Otherwise the hires land in, like, October.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: You can start interviewing. You can't make offers until we cross the line.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Fair.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. So that's the rule. Two more engineers only if ARR passes $9 million by the end of June.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: I'll send the revised budget sheet with all of this by Friday, May 16th.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Thanks, Maya.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Can the sheet show headcount cost separately? It helps me when I put offers together.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yes, I'll break out headcount on its own tab.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: And travel?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Travel is flat. Same as Q2. Please don't make me regret that.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: No promises.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Maya, one more question on budget. What does the reserve look like? If something goes wrong in Q3, how much room do we actually have?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: We hold a contingency inside the 1.2. It's small. I'd rather not touch it before August.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Does the contingency cover the maps thing? I know we're coming to that at the end.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Let's hold that for risks. Short answer, partly.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: And tools. We're paying for two applicant tracking systems right now because the migration never finished.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Oh, I didn't know that. How much is the old one?

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: A few hundred a month. Not huge, but it's silly.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Cancel it once the migration is done. Please.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: I'll finish the migration this month.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Same for support. We have a chat tool nobody uses anymore. I'll check when it renews and turn it off.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Thank you. Honestly, this is how the budget stays flat. It's all the small things.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Can I ask about the website rebuild? It was in the Q2 plan and it slipped.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: It's not in Q3. If marketing wants it, it comes out of the 310.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Okay. Then it waits. The launch matters more than the website.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Agreed. The website rebuild waits.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: On cloud, I want to be honest that the log change won't fix everything. The search cluster is oversized for what we use, and resizing it means a maintenance window, probably a Saturday night.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: How much does resizing save?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: I don't have a number yet. I'll put it in the offline spec next to the infrastructure estimate, since it's the same people looking at it.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Fine. As long as I see it before the budget sheet goes out.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Good. Let's move to hiring. Kofi.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Okay. So we have seven open roles right now.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Three engineers, two support specialists, one product designer, and one product manager. The engineering roles have been open the longest, and the pipeline for those is, uh, thin, honestly. We get a lot of applicants but very few with the right background.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: And the designer role, is that the backfill for, uh, the design lead?

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: No, the design lead is filled. That's the good news. Lena Okafor accepted on Monday.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: She starts June 9th.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Oh, that's great.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Nice. Finally. We've been without a design lead since January.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: The designer role is a separate mid-level role, it reports to Lena.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Got it. How is time to fill looking?

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: The average is 45 days right now. Engineering is longer, more like sixty.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: For the offline work, I'd really like one of the three engineers to have mobile sync experience.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: I can rewrite the job description. Is that a must-have or a nice-to-have?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Must-have for one of them. Nice-to-have for the other two.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Okay. That will make the one role slower, just so you know. There aren't many of those people.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: I know. I'd rather wait for the right person.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: The two support roles are the ones I really need. We are, um, we're drowning, honestly.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: I know. Those listings aren't posted yet because we were waiting on the budget.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Support headcount is in the budget. You can post them.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Great. Then I'll post both support listings by May 12th.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: May 12th. Good.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Can the listings mention the shift times? Last time half the candidates didn't realize it was West Coast hours.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Yes. I'll put the hours in the first line.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: What about the PM role? Do we actually need it in Q3?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: I'd argue yes. Someone has to own the mobile app, and right now that's, um, nobody.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: I'd argue we could wait. Offline mode has a clear spec, it doesn't need a new PM in the middle of it.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: I can see both sides.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Let's keep the PM role open but not prioritize it. Kofi, recruit for engineering and support first.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Understood. Engineering and support first, then the PM, then the designer.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Does the designer wait for Lena?

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: I think it should. She should pick her own hire.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Agreed. We don't start the designer search until Lena is in.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: One more thing on hiring. The referral bonus is going up to $3,000 starting this quarter.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: That'll help. Most of our good engineers came from referrals.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: And the interview panels. I need engineers to actually accept the invites.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: I'll say something at standup. Fair point.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Kofi, what's the offer approval process going to be? Last quarter offers sat with me for a week, and I know that was on me.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: I'd like a two day turnaround. If finance hasn't replied in two days, I follow up with Helen.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: That's fine with me. Maya, does that work for you?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yes. I'll block time on Tuesdays and Thursdays just for offers.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: And can we use the same take-home exercise for all three engineering roles? It saves a lot of interviewer time.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: For two of them, yes. The mobile sync role should have its own exercise.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Okay. I'll ask one of the mobile engineers to write it.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: For support interviews, I want a writing exercise. Half the job is writing clear replies to upset customers.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: That's a good idea. A short reply to a real, anonymized ticket?

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Exactly. Twenty minutes, no more than that.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Can marketing help with the employer brand side? The careers page is, um, pretty bad right now.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Yes, please. Anything is better than what's there.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: I'll have someone on my team refresh the careers page copy. Nothing fancy.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Kofi, how are we doing on interview feedback? Last quarter some candidates waited two weeks to hear back, and one of them wrote about it publicly.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: I remember. The new rule is feedback in the system within one business day of the interview, and I chase anyone who misses it. It's been better this month.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: My team is the worst offender, I know. I'll remind them again.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Anything else on hiring?

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: No, that's it.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. The launch. Arjun, you said you had thoughts.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Yeah. So, um, I don't think June 2nd holds.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: We found two sync bugs in the offline prototype last week, and one of them can lose data.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Lose data how?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: If two technicians edit the same job while they're both offline, the second sync overwrites the first one. Silently.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Oh. That's bad.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: It's bad. We have a fix designed, but it needs about two weeks of testing. The fix itself is not complicated, it's the testing that takes time, because we have to simulate a lot of devices going on and offline in different orders.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Two weeks is going to hurt. The press briefings are booked for the week of June 2nd.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Can we move them?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Probably. Two of the three are flexible. I'd rather move them than launch with a data loss bug.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Agreed. Nobody wants that headline.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: So what date are you proposing?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: June 16th. That gives us the two weeks of testing plus a few days of buffer.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Does anyone object to June 16th?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Not from finance. Some marketing spend shifts into the second half of June, but that's fine.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Lena starts on the ninth, so she'd be around for launch week. That's probably good.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Then that's the decision. The 3.0 launch moves from June 2nd to June 16th.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Okay. I'll update the launch announcement and the press plan by May 23rd.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Thanks. And the beta?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: The beta still starts May 27th, with 50 customers. That doesn't change.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Who picks the 50?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Tobias and I were going to pick from the customer advisory board.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Can I add a few? I know which customers file the most offline complaints. They'd be great testers.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Yes, please. Send me names.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: I'll send you ten names by the end of the week.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Make sure they're customers who'll actually give feedback, not just complain.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Those are the same people, honestly.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Do the beta customers get the data loss fix?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Yes, the beta build has the fix. That's partly why we need the beta, to see it under real conditions.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: And if the beta finds something else serious?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Then I'll tell you within a day, and we talk about the date again. But I don't expect it.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Tobias, the press plan should say June 16th everywhere, including the website banner.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Yes. The banner currently says "early June." I'll change it.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: And the launch event budget, does that move too?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: The venue is booked for the 16th already, oddly enough. We had it as a backup date.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Lucky. Okay. Anything else on the launch?

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Is there a launch party? Asking for the whole office.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: There will be cake. That's all I'll commit to.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: One more launch thing, sorry. Release notes. Who writes them this time?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Marketing writes the announcement, but the release notes should come from engineering. You know what actually changed.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Okay. I'll have one of the leads draft them, and Tobias can edit for tone.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Support needs the release notes at least a week ahead. We have to update the help center before customers start asking.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: A week ahead of the 16th. Okay, noted.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: And training for the support team on offline mode?

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: We'd want a session during the beta, so we're learning alongside the beta customers, not after launch.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: I can run that. An hour, with the prototype.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Can the temps join that session? If they're starting around then.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Wait, what temps? Oh, right, we haven't got there yet. Yes, if they're on board by then.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: What's the rollback plan if the launch goes badly?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Offline mode ships behind a flag. If something breaks, we turn it off for everyone and the app works the way it does today.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Good. That's what I wanted to hear.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: For the announcement itself, I want one customer quote about offline mode. Ideally someone from the beta who's actually used it in a basement or out in a rural area.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: I have a few customers in mind, the water utility people especially. Their technicians are underground half the day.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Perfect. Introduce me once the beta starts and they've had a week with it.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Just make sure we get written approval for any quote. Legal will ask, they always do.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Support backlog. Beatriz.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Okay. So, the backlog is at 1,340 open tickets. That's up from about 900 in February.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Wow.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Yeah. The median first response time is 14 hours. Our target is four hours.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Fourteen hours?

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Fourteen. On weekends it's worse. The team is doing their best, but it's the same five people, and they're tired. I've had two people ask me about transferring to other teams this month.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: And about a third of the backlog is duplicates of the same three bugs. The sync one, the recurring jobs one, and the login loop on Android.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: The login loop is fixed in the next build. It goes out Thursday.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Great. Then that's maybe 150 tickets I can close with one macro.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: What else do you need?

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Two things. Short term, two temporary support agents for six weeks through the agency. Long term, the two hires Kofi is posting.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: What does the temp option cost?

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: About $24,000 total for both of them, for the six weeks.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: That fits. It's within the support line.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Decision: we bring on two temporary support agents for six weeks.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Thank you. Really.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: And from engineering, I'll put two engineers on a bug rotation, rotating weekly, just for support escalations.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: That would help a lot. Right now escalations sit for days.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Does that come out of the offline mode 40 percent?

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: No. Keep offline mode at 40. The rotation comes out of the other 60.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Okay. That works.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Beatriz, I want to see whether this is working. Can you send a backlog report every week?

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Yes. I'll send a weekly backlog report every Monday, starting May 19th.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Good. What should the report show?

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Open tickets, median first response, and the top five ticket categories.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Can it show the temp agents separately? So we know if they're worth renewing.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Sure, I'll split it by agent type.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Do the temps need laptops? IT takes like two weeks.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Oh. Yes. Kofi, can you start that?

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: I'll flag it to IT today.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Is there anything we should say to customers? Like a status note about response times?

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: I'd rather not announce it. I'd rather just get faster.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Agreed. No announcement. Let's fix it quietly.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: And can we stop sending the satisfaction survey for a few weeks? Right now it's just collecting angry replies.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Hmm. I'd rather keep it. It's useful data even when it's angry.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Okay. Fair.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Beatriz, are the duplicate tickets tagged? If they're tagged, I can tell the rotation engineers which bug matters most.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Mostly. The Android ones are tagged well. The sync ones are messy, people describe them twenty different ways.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Could we add a sync problem option to the in-app help form? Then customers would tag themselves.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Yes. That would save us a lot of triage time.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: It's small. I'll get it into the build after Thursday's.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: What about the help center? Do we have articles for the top bugs?

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: For two of the three. The recurring jobs one doesn't have an article because we kept thinking it would be fixed.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Write it anyway. Even if it's fixed in a month.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Okay. Will do.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: And weekend coverage? You said weekends are worse.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Right now it's one person on Saturdays and nobody on Sundays. The temps would let us cover Sundays.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Is Sunday coverage part of the $24,000?

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Yes, it's included in that.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Beatriz, what happens when the six weeks are up? I don't want the backlog to come straight back the week the temps leave.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: The plan is that by then the two permanent hires are trained, and the duplicate tickets are gone because the bugs are fixed. If either of those slips, I'll come back and ask.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Ask early if you do. Extending through the agency takes about two weeks of notice.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Anything else on support?

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: No. Thanks, everyone.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay, last section, risks. We have about five minutes, so let's go fast.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: The big one is maps. Northgate Maps told us their API price is going up 30 percent on July 1st.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Thirty percent? On what we pay now, that's, um, about $54,000 more a year.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Do we have alternatives?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Tessera Geo is the one I'd look at. Their routing is decent and they have an offline tiles option, which actually fits offline mode really well. Switching is not trivial though. We'd have to redo the map layer in both apps, which is probably three or four weeks of work for one engineer.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Is switching visible to customers?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: A little. The map style changes. The data's about the same.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Decision: we start evaluating Tessera Geo as a replacement for Northgate. We're not committing to switch yet.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: I'll get a quote from Tessera Geo by June 13th.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Ask them for a two year price lock. That's the whole point.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: Will do.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Second risk: the SOC 2 audit. It's on August 18th, and two of the big prospects are waiting on the report.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Three, actually. The hospital network asked again yesterday.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Okay, three. I own the evidence collection.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: I'll have the SOC 2 evidence package ready by July 25th.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Do you need help?

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: I'll need about a day from each team lead. I'll send the requests out.

segments.speaker: Kofi
segments.text: Third risk, maybe. Lena starts June 9th, a week before launch. That's a rough first week.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Fair. Tobias, can you make sure she's not thrown straight into launch assets?

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: Yeah. I'll protect her calendar.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: And one from me. If we miss the ARR target, Arjun's team is stretched all quarter.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: I know. That's why we cut scope at the start of this meeting.

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: There's also a smaller one. Our Android build tooling is two versions behind, and the app store will require the new one by the fall.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Is that a Q3 problem?

segments.speaker: Arjun
segments.text: It's a Q3 problem if we leave it. It's about a week of work. I'll fit it into the rotation.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: And the hospital network wants a security questionnaire before the SOC 2 report is even done.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Send it to me. I've already answered most of those questions for the audit.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: On maps, can we pass any of the increase on to customers? Some of our contracts have a clause for third-party costs.

segments.speaker: Tobias
segments.text: I'd really rather not. We're about to launch, and a price change in the same month sends the wrong message.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Agreed. Let's see what the Tessera Geo quote looks like first, then decide.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Okay. Last thing. I'm going to schedule a risk review for June 30th, after the launch.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: We'll check on maps, the SOC 2 work, and the backlog.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: June 30th works for me.

segments.speaker: Beatriz
segments.text: Works for me too.

segments.speaker: Helen
segments.text: Good. That's time. Thanks, everyone. I know a few of these were hard calls, especially in the first half, so I appreciate everyone being straightforward about it. Great session.
